metrology.measurement_stats.title: Summary statistics of repeated measurements (repeatability)

variables.name: measurements
variables.desc: list of repeated measurements in the same unit (m)

assumptions: Sample standard deviation with the n − 1 denominator.
method_references: Sample mean, standard deviation and range

metrology.measurement_uncertainty.title: Combined and expanded measurement uncertainty
assumptions: Independent contributions combined in quadrature; k = 2 gives ~95% coverage for a normal distribution.
method_references: GUM combined uncertainty u_c = √(u_A² + u_B²); U = k·u_c (recalled)

metrology.gauge_rr.title: Gauge R&R study (AIAG method, K-constants from computed d2/d2*)

variables.name: n_trials
variables.desc: number of repeated trials per appraiser per part

variables.name: k_sigma
variables.desc: sigma-spread multiplier for the range (5.15 for 99 %, 6 for 99.73 %)

variables.name: R_bar
variables.desc: average of the trial ranges (over all appraisers and parts)

variables.name: X_bar_diff
variables.desc: range of the appraiser part-averages (max − min)

variables.name: tol
variables.desc: tolerance (USL − LSL) or process spread for %Tolerance

procedure.python:
def _gauge_rr(values):
    r = int(values['n_trials'])
    a = int(values['n_appraisers'])
    p_ = int(values['n_parts'])
    k = values['k_sigma']
    # K1 uses the plain d2 (R̄ is an average of many trial ranges, g = appraisers × parts).
    K1 = k / _d2_d3(r)[0]
    # K2 and K3 come from a SINGLE range (the appraiser-average range and the part-average range, g = 1),
    # so they use d2* = √(d2² + d3²).
    K2 = k / _d2_star(a)
    K3 = k / _d2_star(p_)
    Rbar = values['R_bar']
    EV = Rbar * K1
    # Reproducibility: appraiser variation, corrected for the repeatability embedded in X̄_diff.
    AV2 = (values['X_bar_diff'] * K2) ** 2 - EV ** 2 / (r * p_)
    AV = math.sqrt(max(0.0, AV2))
    GRR = math.sqrt(EV ** 2 + AV ** 2)
    PV = values['R_p'] * K3
    TV = math.sqrt(GRR ** 2 + PV ** 2)
    tol = values['tol']
    if tol <= 0:
        raise MechError('tol must be positive')
    return {'EV': EV, 'AV': AV, 'GRR': GRR, 'PV': PV, 'TV': TV,
            'pct_GRR_TV': 100.0 * GRR / TV, 'pct_GRR_Tol': 100.0 * GRR / tol,
            'ndc': 1.41 * PV / GRR}

assumptions: AIAG method: K1 = k_sigma/d2(trials) uses the plain d2 (R̄ averages many ranges), while K2 = k_sigma/d2*(appraisers) and K3 = k_sigma/d2*(parts) use d2* = √(d2² + d3²) because X̄_diff and R_p are each a single range (g = 1). d2 and d3 are computed by numeric integration of the range distribution. AV is corrected for the repeatability embedded in X̄_diff. %GRR < 10% acceptable, 10–30% marginal, >30% unacceptable.
method_references: AIAG Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), gauge R&R (recalled)

metrology.cp_cpk.title: Process capability Cp and Cpk (short-term sigma)

variables.name: Cpk
variables.desc: process capability index Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ)

assumptions: Cp measures potential (centered); Cpk reflects the nearer limit and is NEGATIVE when the process mean falls outside the specification (a signed index). Requires USL > LSL.
method_references: Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ); Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ) (recalled)

metrology.pp_ppk.title: Process performance Pp and Ppk (overall sigma)

variables.name: Ppk
variables.desc: process performance index Ppk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ_t)

assumptions: Pp/Ppk use the overall (long-term) sigma; Cp/Cpk use the within-subgroup sigma. Ppk is signed (negative when the mean is outside the specification).
method_references: Pp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ_t); Ppk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ_t) (recalled)

metrology.control_chart_constants.title: Control chart constants A2, D3, D4, d2, d3 (computed from the range distribution)

variables.name: d2
variables.desc: mean of the range of n standard normals (E[R])

variables.name: d3
variables.desc: standard deviation of the range of n standard normals

procedure.python:
def _control_constants(values):
    n = int(values['n'])
    d2, d3 = _d2_d3(n)
    A2 = 3.0 / (d2 * math.sqrt(n))
    D3 = max(0.0, 1.0 - 3.0 * d3 / d2)
    D4 = 1.0 + 3.0 * d3 / d2
    return {'d2': d2, 'd3': d3, 'A2': A2, 'D3': D3, 'D4': D4}

assumptions: d2 and d3 are computed by numeric integration of the range distribution of n iid standard normals (not from a recalled table): d2(2) = 2/√π exactly.
method_references: Statistical definitions d2 = E[R], d3 = √Var[R]; A2 = 3/(d2√n), D3/D4 = 1 ∓ 3d3/d2 (recalled)

metrology.control_limits_xbar_r.title: X̄ and R chart control limits (from computed A2/D3/D4)

variables.name: X_bar_bar
variables.desc: grand mean (center of the X̄ chart)

variables.name: R_bar
variables.desc: average range (center of the R chart)

assumptions: UCL_x = X̄̄ + A2·R̄, LCL_x = X̄̄ − A2·R̄; R chart UCL/LCL = D4·R̄ / D3·R̄. A2, D3, D4 are computed (see control_chart_constants). A negative LCL_x means no lower limit.
method_references: Shewhart X̄ and R chart limits (recalled)

metrology.control_limits_p.title: p-chart (fraction nonconforming) control limits
assumptions: Control limits p̄ ± 3√(p̄(1−p̄)/n), with LCL = max(0, …) and UCL = min(1, …) — a p-chart cannot have a negative lower limit or an upper limit above 1.

metrology.sigma_level.title: Process sigma level from long-term yield (Z_lt and Z_st)

variables.name: yield
variables.desc: first-pass yield of LONG-TERM (shifted) data (fraction conforming, 0..1)

assumptions: The yield of long-term (shifted) process data gives the long-term sigma level directly, Z_lt = Φ⁻¹(yield); the short-term level removes the conventional 1.5σ shift, Z_st = Z_lt + 1.5. Landmark: yield = 0.99865 (1350 DPMO) → Z_lt = 3, Z_st = 4.5.
method_references: Z_lt = Φ⁻¹(yield); Z_st = Z_lt + 1.5 (Six Sigma convention, recalled)

metrology.sigma_level_dpmo.title: Process sigma level from DPMO (Z_lt and Z_st)

variables.name: Z_lt
variables.desc: long-term sigma level Z_lt = Φ⁻¹(1 − dpmo/1e6)

assumptions: DPMO → yield = 1 − dpmo/10⁶, then Z_lt = Φ⁻¹(yield) and Z_st = Z_lt + 1.5. Landmark: 3.4 DPMO → Z_lt = 4.5, Z_st = 6.0.
method_references: DPMO → sigma level; Z_st = Z_lt + 1.5 (Six Sigma convention, recalled)

metrology.acceptance_sampling.title: Acceptance probability and AOQ for a single sampling plan (finite lot, hypergeometric)
assumptions: Hypergeometric model (sampling without replacement); D = round(p·N). AOQ assumes rejected lots are 100% inspected (rectification).

metrology.oc_binomial.title: Acceptance probability for a single sampling plan (infinite lot, binomial)
assumptions: Binomial model (large/infinite lot or sampling with replacement).

metrology.gauge_blocks.title: Gauge-block combination for a target length (minimum block count)

variables.name: selected
variables.desc: block sizes that sum to the target, in m (largest first)

procedure.python:
def _gauge_blocks(values):
    """Gauge-block combination by minimum-block-count dynamic programming.

    Sizes are scaled to 0.5 µm so 0.0005 mm blocks are representable exactly. The 0/1 knapsack DP stores
    the fewest blocks that reach each length, so among several exact stacks the one using the fewest
    blocks is returned (e.g. target 5 mm from {1..5} mm → {5}, not {3+2}).
    """
    import numpy as np
    target = values['target']
    if target < 0:
        raise MechError('target must be non-negative')
    scale = 2e6  # 0.5 um per unit
    T = int(round(target * scale))
    if T > 4_000_000:
        raise MechError('target too large for an exact combination (limit 2 m)')
    raw = [float(b) for b in values['blocks'] if float(b) > 0]
    if not raw:
        raise MechError('blocks: give a non-empty list of positive block sizes')
    # Largest blocks first: a DP stage only claims a length when it strictly improves it, so on ties between equally
    # short stacks the larger blocks win (conventional wringing practice, e.g. 6 mm → {5, 1} rather than {4, 2}).
    blocks = sorted(set(int(round(b * scale)) for b in raw), reverse=True)
    INF = 1 << 30
    dp = np.full(T + 1, INF, dtype=np.int64)
    dp[0] = 0
    # 0/1 knapsack: the right-hand side is evaluated from the previous stage before assignment, so each block is
    # used at most once. For reconstruction keep, per block stage, a bit-packed mask of the lengths that stage
    
    # could reuse a block, e.g. {1,2,3,4} → 9 gave [4, 4, 1].]
    improved = []
    for b in blocks:
        cand = np.full(T + 1, INF, dtype=np.int64)
        if b <= T:
            cand[b:] = dp[:-b] + 1
        better = cand < dp
        improved.append(np.packbits(better))
        dp = np.where(better, cand, dp)
    if dp[T] >= INF:
        raise MechError('no exact combination of the given blocks reaches the target')
    selected = []
    r = T
    for i in range(len(blocks) - 1, -1, -1):
        if r == 0:
            break
        if np.unpackbits(improved[i], count=T + 1)[r]:
            selected.append(blocks[i] / scale)
            r -= blocks[i]
    if r != 0:
        raise MechError('internal reconstruction error')
    return {'selected': sorted(selected, reverse=True), 'residual': r / scale, 'n_blocks': len(selected)}

assumptions: Each block used at most once; sizes resolved to 0.5 µm. Among the exact stacks, the one using the FEWEST blocks is returned (target 5 mm from {1..5} mm → {5}, not {3+2}). Raises an error when no exact combination exists.
method_references: Gauge-block stacking by minimum-count subset-sum dynamic programming
